title: Fuzzing Methodology and Campaign Design
markdown:
**Fuzzing methodology** is how you turn ad-hoc fuzzer runs into a **repeatable security program**: choosing targets, building harnesses and corpora, running with **sanitizers**, measuring **coverage**, triaging crashes into **actionable bugs**, and closing the loop with **fixes and regression seeds**. This guide complements **[Fuzzing Security Testing](../Fuzzing%20Security%20Testing/)** (harness mechanics and tools).

Aligned with the **[Content Mastery Framework](../Interview%20Preparation/Content%20Mastery%20Framework.md)**.

|-------|------------------------|----------------|
| **Coverage-guided mutation** | Bit-flip/arith/splice on seeds with edge feedback | Opaque binary formats, C/C++ parsers |

| **Differential fuzzing** | Same input, compare two implementations | Crypto, image codecs, JSON parsers |

children.title: Misconceptions
“Just leave the fuzzer running forever.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **Diminishing returns** are normal. Stagnation means you should **change inputs or strategy**, not only add CPU hours.
children.notes: Reality: Diminishing returns are normal. Stagnation means you should change inputs or strategy, not only add CPU hours.
children.blurb: Reality: Diminishing returns are normal.

children.title: “Raw crash count is our KPI.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **Unique defects fixed**, **coverage growth**, and **regression prevention** outperform **duplicate** crash totals.
children.notes: Reality: Unique defects fixed, coverage growth, and regression prevention outperform duplicate crash totals.
children.blurb: Reality: Unique defects fixed, coverage growth, and regression prevention...

children.title: “Security owns fuzzing end-to-end.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **Engineering** fixes code and often **co-builds** harnesses. Security sets **risk priority**, **bar**, and **verification**.
children.notes: Reality: Engineering fixes code and often co-builds harnesses. Security sets risk priority, bar, and verification.
children.blurb: Reality: Engineering fixes code and often co-builds harnesses.

children.title: “Fuzzing replaces code review.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **Complementary**. Fuzzing finds many **memory** and **parser** issues; **authorization**, **business logic**, and **race** conditions still need human review and targeted tests.
children.notes: Reality: Complementary. Fuzzing finds many memory and parser issues; authorization, business logic, and race conditions still need human review and targeted tests.
children.blurb: Reality: Complementary.

children.title: “We can fuzz production traffic captures as seeds.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **PII** and **contractual** constraints often forbid this. Prefer **scrubbed** or **synthetic** corpora.
children.notes: Reality: PII and contractual constraints often forbid this. Prefer scrubbed or synthetic corpora.
children.blurb: Reality: PII and contractual constraints often forbid this.

children.title: “No crashes means we can stop fuzzing.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **New code**, **compiler changes**, and **config drift** reopen surface. Campaigns should be **continuous** or **regression-gated** in CI.
children.notes: Reality: New code, compiler changes, and config drift reopen surface. Campaigns should be continuous or regression-gated in CI.
children.blurb: Reality: New code, compiler changes, and config drift reopen surface.

children.title: “One global job covers all products.”
children.markdown: **Reality:** **Per-component** harnesses and **owners** scale; monolithic jobs hide accountability and **delay** fixes.
children.notes: Reality: Per-component harnesses and owners scale; monolithic jobs hide accountability and delay fixes.

children.markdown: **Reality:** **Specs evolve**. Stale grammars **miss** new branches; they need **versioning** like production parsers.

children.title: Interview prompts
60-second answer
children.markdown:
**Q: How do you run fuzzing as a program, not a one-off?**

**A:** I start with a **risk-weighted inventory** of parsers and native components, then assign **named owners** and **SLAs** for security-relevant crashes. Each target gets a **harness**, **seed corpus**, and **sanitizer** build where possible; jobs run **continuously or on a tight cadence** with **coverage** and **deduped crash** metrics. I work with engineering on **minimized repros**, **root-cause fixes**, and **regression inputs** checked into tests. Leadership sees **edges over time**, **mean time to fix** for crashers, and **open S0/S1** items-not vanity crash totals.

children.title: Q: How do you know a campaign is “stuck”?
children.markdown: **A:** **Coverage plateau** (no new edges over a meaningful window) with **low unique crash rate**, or crashes **cluster** to known **won't-fix** buckets. Response: **refresh seeds**, add **dictionary** tokens, try **structure-aware** generation, or **refactor** the harness API to unlock new paths.

children.title: CI and scale
Q: Should every PR run a full fuzz job?
children.markdown: **A:** Usually **no**-full campaigns are **too slow**. Typical pattern: **nightly** full pools plus **PR-gated** **smoke** (short runs, **regression** corpus only, or **affected-target** subset).
